full_judgment:
2. The facts in short are that the appellants in CA No. 8 of 2005 i.e. Mohiuddin Khan and another as plaintiff filed the above Title Suit No.16 of 1992 on 6-2-1992 against the heirs of Shihamul Haque since deceased and others stating, inter alia, that they by kabala Nos.1586, 1588, 1589 and 1600 dated 1-2-1974, 15-2-1974, 11-2-1974 and 14-2-1974 respectively purchased 0.54 acres of land appertaining to CS Plot No.248 of CS khatian No.235 corresponding to SA khatian No.406 of Mouza Chandana PS Joydebpur, District-Gazipur described in schedule 'A' of the plaint from Chaturi Tanti and got delivery of possession and by Mutation Case No.170/74-75 their names were mutated in SA Khatian No.406 in place of said Chaturi Tanti and they paid ground rents and got dakhilas. Against the above order of mutation, Shihamul Haque preferred Misc. Appeal Case No.13 of 1981 claiming title on the basis of deed of exchange (settlement) dated 16-6-1980 and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, by order dated 12-1-1982, without at all giving any finding as to possession of the suit land, cancelled the mutation. The appellants then filed Appeal No.8 of 1982 and the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka who heard the appeal, having found that the appellants and others were in possession of the case land, set aside the above order dated 12-1-1982 and restored the mutation in the name of appellants and others. Then Shihamul Haque preferred Appeal No.96 of 1984 before the Board of Land Administration and after hearing the same was dismissed. Shihamul Haque then filed Writ Petition No.159 of 1989 and the High Court Division, after hearing declared that the above orders passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka and the Board of Land Administration are without any lawful authority with the observation that the question of title and ownership and validity of the deeds in question could be gone into and decided only by a civil court. the appellants out of the proceedings of the above Misc. Appeal Case No.13 of 1981 and also from the contents of the annexures of the above Writ Petition No.159 of 1989 for the first time came to know about the alleged deed of agreement for exchange dated 30-10-1963, the alleged powers of attorneys dated 7-6-1965, the deed of exchange dated 16-6-1980 in terms of Exchange Case No.35/69-70, Title Suit Nos.27 of 1971 and 150 of 1972, Civil Revision Nos.315 and 1387 of 1977 and also of the withdrawals of the same on 29-1-1980 and 21-1-1980 which were referred in the above proceeding. The appellants are bonafide purchasers of the suit land for valuable consideration without any notice of agreement of exchange and other facts as stated above. Ordinance No.1 of 1964 (EP Disturbed Persons Rehabilitation Ordinance, 1964) having died by the efflux of time on 31-12-1964 as held in 17 DLR 451, the above proceeding of Exchange Case No.35/69-70 stated on 24-7-1969 for forfeiting the land of the appellants for the purpose of granting so-called settlement is without jurisdiction. The possession of the property in question was always with the appellants and was never taken over by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka or Sub-Divisional Officer and the same was never enlisted in the Census List of 1966-1967. 

 4. The appellants in CA No.  9 of 2005 i.e. Sree Monmohan Shaha and another as plaintiff on 25-2-1992 filed the above Title Suit No.  25 of 1992 against the heirs of Shihamul Haque and others claiming similar relief on more or less similar averments made in the above Title Suit No. 16 of 1992, variation being that the area of the suit land was 0.98 acres as described in Schedule A, B and C of the plaint, the appellant No. 1 purchased from Shibulal Tanti 0.02 acres of land of Plot No. 1952 of Khatian No. 68, 0.35 acres of land of Plot No. 1905 of Khatian No. 290, 0.05 acres of land of Plot No. 1916 of Khatian No. 429 i.e. total 0.06 acres, all within the said mouza Chandana by registered kabalas dated 24-1-1979 and appellant No. 2 also purchased 0.06 acres of land of the aforesaid Plot No. 1916 and some other land from aforesaid Plot No. 1952 by registered kabala dated 6-1-1979 from the aforesaid Shibulal Tanti and they were put into possession of the suit land immediately. They had filed the Separation and Mutation Case No. 1384 of 1978-79 in the office of CO (Rev) Joydebpur and their names were mutated in SA Khatian Nos.  68,290 and 429 under the order of CO (Rev) dated 19-6-1979 and they have been paying ground rent for the suit lands since 6-9-1979. The plaint of the above suit also contained averments regarding filing of Misc. Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, Appeal No. 8 of 1982 before Additional Commissioner, Appeal No. 96 of 1984 before Board of Land Administration and Writ Petition No. 159 of 1989 before the High Court Division and in the above suit the defendant Nos. 1(a)-1(d), the heirs of Shihamul Haque also filed written statement making averments similar to in their written statement filed in Title Suit No. 16 of 1992. The trial court by judgment and decree dated 16-2-1995 dismissed both Title Suit Nos. 16 and 25 of 1992. The appellants preferred First Appeal Nos. 108 and 203 of 1995 and the High Court Division after hearing dismissed both the appeals holding, inter alia, that Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka was competent and legally authorized to execute and register the deed of exchange (settlement) and it is not necessary that the property should be declared either as enemy property or vested property for its vesting upon the government for regularizing the pending genuine exchange cases including the instant one. The plaintiff-appellants having not filed the suits within three years from the date of knowledge of the settlement deed as required under Article 91 of the Limitation act, the suits are hopelessly barred by limitation. The plaintiff-appellants, during the pendency of the suits/civil revisions which were admittedly filed by their vendors made the purchases without the permission of the court and so the above purchases of the plaintiffs are hit by the principles of lis pendens as provided under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act. The plaintiff appellants having not paid proper court fees as required for the several reliefs as sought, the suits are also hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and section 7 of the Court Fees Act. After withdrawal of the suit or dismissal of a suit for non-prosecution for default no fresh suit can be filed by the same parties or any party claiming through them on the same subject of dispute without the permission of the court and as the earlier suits including the civil revisions being dismissed for non-prosecution, the present suits being filed without obtaining permissions, are not, maintainable.
